key_insight: Structure-preserving finite element discretizations retain topology-controlled long-time behavior of advected differential forms and, under spectral-preservation conditions, exclude spurious dynamo growth.
engineering_relevance: These guarantees support reliable long-duration advection–diffusion simulations where artificial growth or incorrect steady states would undermine predictions.
method: Use a weighted Hodge decomposition to characterize potential-flow limits through harmonic forms and Betti numbers.
Construct a mixed finite element exterior calculus scheme that preserves closed stationary modes.
Establish discrete antidynamo results using spectral approximation or lowest-order exponential-fitting M-matrix discretization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical guarantees, including exponential convergence of numerical 1-forms on two-dimensional manifolds for every positive diffusion coefficient, rather than empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Discrete antidynamo guarantees require spectral preservation; arbitrary-mesh validity is established for the specified lowest-order exponential-fitting discretization, not generic FEEC schemes.
paper_title: Long-time asymptotics of advection-diffusion of finite element differential forms
